subject.title: feat(apps): rewind and fork a session from native chat bubbles

question: Is the native macOS/iOS runtime proof sufficient to accept these new session-mutating bubble actions once it is posted?
rationale: The branch adds visible controls that alter session state, while the supplied evidence is automated-test-only and the protected maintainer label requires an explicit human merge judgment.

options.title: Request native runtime proof
options.body: Require a redacted simulator or Desktop recording showing an eligible user bubble, busy-state disablement, rewind refresh/composer seed, and fork navigation before merge.

options.title: Accept test-only evidence
options.body: A maintainer may accept the focused Swift and protocol coverage without visual runtime proof, explicitly owning the native interaction risk.

recommendation.title: Request native runtime proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted simulator or Desktop recording showing an eligible user bubble, busy-state disablement, rewind refresh/composer seed, and fork navigation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the merged underlying rewind/fork behavior and authored the native follow-up implementation.
